description: "Somewhere, something incredible is waiting to be known."
summary:
FLAME / ATLAS is a web dashboard that helps people explore NASA research on fire in microgravity.
NASA has studied how different materials burn, how smoke behaves, and how flames can be extinguished in space, but the findings are spread across many experiments.
Our project brings 16 NASA PSI investigations into one searchable place. Users can filter studies, compare experiments, explore ISS, Moon, and Mars mission scenarios, and follow links back to original NASA sources.
We also built an evidence-based assistant and a CSV tool for inspecting experimental measurements. The ranking helps users find research that is relevant to a question; it is not a prediction of fire risk.
FLAME / ATLAS is designed to make spacecraft fire-safety research easier to understand and use, especially for students and future space-habitat researchers.
details:
The Problem

Fire is a serious danger during space missions. In microgravity, flames and smoke behave differently than they do on Earth. Understanding these differences is important for protecting astronauts on the ISS and during future missions to the Moon and Mars.

NASA has collected valuable combustion research over many years. However, finding and comparing the most relevant experiments can be difficult, especially for students and people who are new to this topic.

Our Solution

We created FLAME / ATLAS, an interactive website that organizes NASA's microgravity combustion research in one place.

Our dashboard includes 16 investigations from NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository, including BASS, Saffire, SAME, and FLEX.

Users can:

  • Search and filter combustion experiments.
  • Compare studies and their experimental conditions.
  • Explore different mission environments, including the ISS, Moon, and Mars.
  • See which research is most relevant to specific fire safety questions.
  • Import experimental CSV data and explore measurements.
  • Ask a research assistant questions and follow links to NASA sources.

How It Works

Each investigation is described using information from NASA PSI, including research objectives, materials, test conditions, measurements, and possible applications.

We developed a ranking system that helps users identify useful research for different fire safety topics. The scores are based on research relevance, not predicted fire danger.

The dashboard also highlights gaps in available evidence. For example, microgravity experiments cannot directly predict how a fire will behave under lunar or Martian gravity.

Technologies Used

We built the website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Python and FastAPI provide an optional backend for AI-generated research explanations using the OpenAI API.

The public website also includes a research assistant that works without an API key by searching the curated information.

GitHub Pages is used to publish the website.

Why It Matters

Our goal is to make NASA's combustion research easier to access and understand.

FLAME / ATLAS can help students learn about microgravity combustion and help researchers find relevant experiments for future spacecraft and habitat fire safety studies.

The project is a research and educational tool, not a certified fire safety prediction system.
